template_name: Multi-Modal Material Identity Integration via Bayesian Cue Combination
calibration_constraint: Bridge warrant for architectural parameters: FUNCTIONAL (0.50) maximum per pre-panel review

mechanism_chain.process: Occupant perceives architectural material through multiple sensory channels simultaneously: visual texture/color (via ventral visual stream), haptic roughness/temperature/compliance (via somatosensory cortex), acoustic tap/footstep signature (via auditory cortex), olfactory signature (via olfactory bulb → piriform cortex)
mechanism_chain.substrate: Parallel sensory processing in modality-specific cortices

mechanism_chain.process: Brain infers whether multi-modal signals share a common cause (same material) using Bayesian causal inference. If common-cause probability is high (seeing and touching the same surface), signals are integrated; if low (hearing a distant sound while touching a nearby surface), they are segregated.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Posterior parietal cortex; superior temporal sulcus — causal inference computation

mechanism_chain.process: Integrated material percept is formed by reliability-weighted combination (MLE): each channel contributes in proportion to its signal-to-noise ratio. The combined estimate has lower variance than any individual channel.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Cortical multisensory integration areas; reliability weighting via precision-weighted prediction errors

mechanism_chain.process: Multi-modal material percept generates affective response: material identity (wood, stone, metal, fabric) triggers learned evaluative associations and innate biophilic preferences simultaneously
mechanism_chain.substrate: Orbitofrontal cortex (evaluative), insula (interoceptive affect), amygdala (biophilic salience)

mle_precision_gain_visual_haptic.interpretation: Visual + haptic integration improves material roughness/texture discrimination by ~25% (lab estimate 30–40%, architectural discount to 20–30%, midpoint 25%)

olfactory_precision_addition.interpretation: Adding olfactory channel (natural materials) contributes ~10% additional precision gain. Olfactory is a weaker, less reliable channel with lower MLE weight.

total_multimodal_precision_gain.interpretation: Full multi-modal material experience (see + touch + smell) produces ~35% more precise material percept than visual-only

common_cause_threshold.interpretation: Multi-modal integration requires that signals are spatially co-located (within ~30 cm) and temporally coincident (within ~200 ms). This is satisfied for direct material contact but NOT for visual inspection of distant surfaces.

visual_impairment.effect: Reduced visual reliability → higher weight on haptic and auditory channels → MLE automatically compensates. See MSI_INVERSE_EFFECTIVENESS_002.

age_group.effect: Multisensory integration is generally preserved or enhanced in aging (Laurienti et al., 2006). Older adults may benefit MORE from multi-modal material presentation because single-channel reliability degrades with age.

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Body budget state modulates haptic exploration behavior: under allostatic deficit, occupants reduce environmental touch behavior (withdrawal, reduced approach), limiting multi-modal integration opportunities. The precision gain is available only if the occupant ENGAGES with material surfaces.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Perceived control facilitates exploration: occupants with high environmental control are more likely to touch, explore, and engage multiple sensory channels, maximizing multi-modal integration. Low control restricts exploration to visual-only, forfeiting the precision gain.

cross_template_references: MSI_CONGRUENCY_PRINCIPLE_001 — congruency between channels determines whether integration produces positive or negative affect
MSI_INVERSE_EFFECTIVENESS_002 — degraded unisensory channels increase the multi-modal precision gain
VISUAL-I T1 — visual channel parameters for material texture statistics; no double-counting
name: Multi-Modal Material Identity Integration via Bayesian Cue Combination

touchable_surface_fraction.interpretation: Fraction of material surfaces within arm's reach that can be touched during normal use. Higher fraction → more multi-modal integration opportunities → more precise material percepts.

material_authenticity.interpretation: Authentic materials (real wood, stone, metal) produce congruent multi-modal signals. Simulated materials (wood-print laminate, stone-texture vinyl) produce INCONGRUENT signals — visual says 'wood' but haptic says 'plastic'. Incongruence degrades the precision gain and produces negative affect.
